why_the_manifest_and_not_the_texts:
THE TEXTS ARE NOT THE ARCHIVE'S TO RELICENSE. 67 seats, and at least thirty assert CC BY-SA — Perseus and First1KGreek packaging over public-domain editions. One asserts CC BY-NC. One asserts GPL-2.0. The Crimson Hexagonal dataset is CC BY 4.0, and shipping CC BY-SA text inside it would relicense somebody else's work. The NC seat could not go in at all.

AN ARCHIVE THAT MEASURES PROVENANCE ERASURE DOES NOT PERFORM IT ON PERSEUS.

What the manifest carries is what the archive made: which edition was seated, fetched when, normalized how, verified at which loci, and hashing to what. That is the part that makes a claim checkable — 'verified against the seated texts' is unfalsifiable without it — and it carries the licenses as attribution rather than laundering them.
license_class_derivation: license_class IS DERIVED FROM license_verbatim AND THE DERIVATION IS STATED HERE, because a derived field that hides its basis is how the wrong thing gets redistributed. Order is most-restrictive-first: NC, then GPL, then BY-SA, then BY, then Gutenberg, then public domain, then site terms, then other. A SEAT WHOSE PACKAGING IS CC BY-SA OVER A PUBLIC-DOMAIN EDITION CLASSES AS CC BY-SA, because that is what governs redistribution. license_verbatim is always the authority; the class is a convenience and must not be relied on for a licensing decision.

The transcription is Ganjoor's (ganjoor.net), which names its source for each section and states of its texts: 'هم‌اکنون منبع عمدهٔ آثار موجود در این مجموعه منابع آزاد در دسترس همگان است' (the principal source of the works in this collection is free sources available to all), releasing them on the principle 'دگران کاشتند و ما خوردیم، ما بکاریم و دیگران بخورند' (others planted and we ate; we plant and others will eat). Ganjoor's statement is recorded as given; it is not a formal licence.

seats.why_seated: The archive holds the Hebrew Bible (Westminster Leningrad Codex), the Septuagint (Swete), the Greek New Testament and the Dead Sea Scrolls; the canon that kept Enoch and Jubilees whole, and the only one in which they survive complete, was not on the shelf. Its Old Testament is the widest of any church's: Jubilees, Enoch and the three books of Meqabyan are scripture there. The archive's Revelation line reads the apocalypses as a tradition; this is the tradition in which they were kept.
